children: Major Japanese life insurer Japan Post Insurance Co. aims to increase its investment income by more than 40% from fiscal 2025 (which ended in March 2026) through fiscal 2028 to capitalize on rising interest rates, according to President and CEO Toru Onishi.

Onishi also expressed confidence in boosting product sales during an interview with The Yomiuri Shimbun. "Young customers tend to have a higher interest in savings-related insurance products," he said.
The following is excerpted from the interview.
The Yomiuri Shimbun: What are your revenue targets?

Toru Onishi: Our latest medium-term business plan, which spans from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2028, defines this period as its "Growth and Challenge Phase." As interest rates normalize in Japan, we believe there is room to grow our asset management revenue. We want to increase investment income up 90 billion yen from fiscal 2025, bringing it to over 290 billion yen.

We will streamline operations through AI and digitalization to keep our operating expenses in check. Through such efforts, we aim to increase our (annual) adjusted profit (net income excluding non-recurring items) to more than 190 billion yen.
Yomiuri: What do rising interest rates mean for you?
Onishi: Interest rates have reached levels unimaginable just a few years ago. In May, we adjusted our insurance premiums and increased the assumed interest rate.

As interest rates rise, insurance products have begun to offer the value of saving money while preparing for the future. We would like to sincerely convey the appeal of these savings-oriented products to our customers, which is to help them build assets while staying protected.

Young customers tend to have a higher interest in savings-related insurance products. Many people currently believe that the Nippon Individual Savings Account (NISA) investment program offers better returns, but it remains uncertain how the landscape will shift over the next 15 to 20 years. It is prudent to hold a certain percentage of assets in fixed-rate products.
Yomiuri: Japan Post Insurance is seeing the number of policies in force drop. How do you intend to address this challenge?

Onishi: As policy terms lengthen, family structures and living circumstances change. Therefore, we want to provide more opportunities for customers to periodically review their policy details to ensure their coverage still aligns with their current lifestyle. When reviewing policies, we invite customers to bring their family whenever possible. We explain the necessary procedures plainly, allowing the customers and their family to ask questions and clear up concerns together. Through such efforts, we hope these family members will see that Japan Post Insurance is trustworthy, which will help them think about their own insurance coverage. It will also lead to customers recommending Japan Post Insurance to others.
